title: Before and After Teardown: Measurable Website Changes

cover.alt: Conceptual paired website panels showing a cluttered path simplified into a clear action and form.

figures.title: Four kinds of friction, four concrete changes
figures.summary: The shared lesson is to identify a specific obstacle before choosing a redesign treatment.

items.label: Heavy pages
items.detail: Oversized media and extra scripts → compressed assets, fewer scripts, and deferred offscreen images.

items.label: Unclear navigation
items.detail: Ambiguous labels and buried destinations → plain labels and direct paths.

items.label: Missing next step
items.detail: Service information without an action → an explicit contact or estimate route.

items.label: Broken forms
items.detail: Unnecessary fields and silent failures → fewer inputs, working submission, and confirmation.

figures.caption: A schematic summary of the changes discussed in this post; it does not add or independently verify outcome metrics.

figures.title: Check the evidence behind an outcome
figures.summary: A before-and-after claim is easier to assess when the measurement method is explicit.

items.label: Name the source
items.detail: Identify the analytics, test result, or submission record supporting the number.

items.label: Use comparable windows
items.detail: State the before and after periods being compared.

items.label: Label estimates
items.detail: Keep projected results distinct from measured results.

items.label: Record the change
items.detail: Explain what changed so readers can judge the connection to the outcome.

figures.caption: The article distinguishes measured and projected results; this checklist makes that distinction visible.
